newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court upholds CFI opinion on environment project funding.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds CFI opinion on environment project funding.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday the Fifth Environmental Action Programme did not impose any obligation on the European Commission to notify individuals before granting aid to member states.

Italian agricultural concerns were appealing a ruling by the European Court of First Instance which found they had no standing to contest funds awarded by the Commission for an environmental project in the Po delta area.
The appellants - agriculturalists, farmers and fishermen - argued the Commission acted beyond the authority of the Action programme and disregarded Italian law and principles of sound administration.
The court upheld the CFI reasoning that the contested decision was a measure of general scope, with categories of persons viewed generally.
The EC treaty, under article 173, grants standing to natural or legal persons only where they are directly or individually concerned.
The court found no requirement for the Commission to notify the appellants of monies given to member states for local environment projects.
